items.stem: What is a key difference between a lambda and a non-lambda Proc in Ruby?

options.text: A lambda checks argument count and return exits only the lambda
options.rationale: Lambdas enforce arity and their return is local; procs are lax and return from the enclosing method.
Lambdas take arguments; they check their count.

options.text: A proc cannot be stored in a variable
options.rationale: Both can be stored in variables.

options.text: They are identical in all respects
options.rationale: Arity checking and return semantics differ.

items.explanation: Lambdas enforce arity and their return is local; procs are lax and return from the enclosing method.

items.stem: Select TWO sound uses of modules in Ruby.

options.text: Mixing shared instance methods into multiple classes with include
options.rationale: Modules provide mixin behaviour across unrelated classes.
Modules act as namespaces to avoid name clashes.

options.text: Instantiating the module directly with new
Replacing the need for any classes at all
options.rationale: Modules complement classes rather than replace them.

items.explanation: Modules provide mixin behaviour across unrelated classes.

items.stem: Why rescue StandardError rather than Exception in typical Ruby code?

options.text: Rescuing Exception also traps signals and exit, which you usually should not
options.rationale: StandardError is the right base for ordinary errors; Exception is too broad.

options.text: Exception cannot be rescued at all
options.rationale: It can be rescued, which is exactly the danger.
The reason is scope of what is caught, not speed.

options.text: Exception does not include runtime errors
options.rationale: Exception is the superclass of StandardError and its runtime errors.

items.explanation: StandardError is the right base for ordinary errors; Exception is too broad.
